title: Reading and recording moves

D0.outcome: Explains what each part of a move record tells (piece letter, destination, capture, check, castling, promotion) and why the destination square alone is not enough to identify a move.

D1.outcome: Plays a given eight-move score on a board from either colour and rotated boards, and names the piece and squares of a move called out in notation.

D2.outcome: Reconstructs a short game from its score alone (including captures, castling and a promotion) and states the position after a requested move number.

D3.outcome: Records own game move by move, correctly disambiguating moves of two similar pieces, and recovers the position at move 15 from the record without replaying the game.

misconceptions: Two moves to the same square need no extra information in the record.
The record shows whose move it is without the numbering.
sources: docs/reconciliation-pasted-curriculum.md §1 stage 1 (reconstruct a game from notation as a D2 item)
sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §1 (descriptive notation in the source; we teach algebraic)
conditions: Reconstruction from a record works only if every move is legal and unambiguous; ambiguity must be resolved by the disambiguating square or file.
Practising from both colours and on a rotated board is what makes the board vision transfer.
contrasts: Two knights that can both reach the same square: the destination alone does not identify the move.
A record read from White's side only breaks when the board is turned around.
The comment symbols in a printed score (!, ?) do not change what was played.

soft_prereq_notes.FND.PIECE.PAWN.D1: pawn moves are recorded without a piece letter, a frequent first confusion
